title: The 5 Metals That Melt at the Highest Temperatures, Ranked

scenes.text: The five metals hardest to melt, ranked. Number one stays solid at over three thousand degrees.

scenes.label: Molybdenum · 2,623°C
scenes.text: Number five: molybdenum. It melts at twenty-six hundred and twenty-three degrees Celsius, hotter than lava.

scenes.label: Tantalum · 3,017°C
scenes.text: Number four: tantalum. Three thousand and seventeen degrees, so it ends up in phone parts and jet engines.

scenes.label: Osmium · 3,033°C
scenes.text: Number three: osmium. Thirty-three degrees above tantalum, and it is one of the densest elements known.

scenes.label: Rhenium · 3,186°C
scenes.text: Number two: rhenium. Three thousand one hundred and eighty-six degrees, used in rocket engines.

scenes.label: Tungsten · 3,422°C
scenes.text: Number one: tungsten. Thirty-four hundred and twenty-two degrees Celsius, which is why light bulb filaments are made of it.

description:
The five metals with the highest melting points, ranked.
Tungsten holds out until 3,422 degrees Celsius, which is why it glows inside light bulbs without melting.
Which metal would you want to hold?
first_comment: Which metal surprised you most? And what should we rank next?
